title: Publish current Windows driver evidence
requires: Windows CUDA and D3D12 on the same GPU
scope: Rebuild the current clean revision for CUDA and D3D12, execute applicable public-API reference, physical-quality and adverse-lifecycle contracts, and publish revisioned per-driver qualification inputs without hiding failed, missing or unsupported scope.
acceptance: Each submitted driver result pins the clean source revision, driver binary, device, driver and toolchain plus immutable contract hashes.

Applicable trajectory, analytic-quality and adverse-lifecycle contracts are executed on both drivers; failures, missing contracts and unsupported cases remain explicit and cannot certify a capability.
Register the results in the generated per-driver evidence index and verify the index from a Windows checkout without weakening byte-stable contract identity.
evidence: PASS: native parallel-mater-conformance --check-inputs plus 67 Python conformance tests; JSON/XML CRLF normalization is portable while binary hashing remains exact.

PASS: GTX 1080 CUDA at 2b04e55 advertises 49 records; reference 11 passed/19 failed with five repeat 0xc0000006 crashes; equal-fluid quality 18/18 and brick penetration 0.205278 mm at frame 196 pass; exact F5-03 lifecycle checkpoints remain missing.

PASS: GTX 1080 D3D12 at 2b04e55 advertises 10 records; reference 5 passed/12 failed/13 unsupported; brick penetration 0.205278 mm at frame 196 and resource lifecycle pass; graph and equal-fluid tests remain unsupported and exact F5-03 lifecycle checkpoints remain missing.

PASS: conformance/v1/evidence/index-v1.json validates 3/62 capabilities across 5 reports with zero registry failures; Windows records qualify 0/49 CUDA and 0/10 D3D12 without weakening F5-05/F5-06 contracts.
